questions.question:
**The given sentence is divided into three segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'no error' as your answer.**

Soumya will be speak / on 'Stress management' in / London the next week.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **Soumya will be speak**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in the original sentence was introduced when "**be**" was included, which is unnecessary in this context. 
 
• The verb "speak" should be in its base form "**speak**" instead of "speak" with the auxiliary verb "**will be**."
 
• "**will be**" is used in the future continuous tense. It indicates an ongoing or continuous action that will be happening at a particular point in the future.
 
• "**will + verb**" is used in the simple future tense. It indicates an action that will take place in the future without any additional duration or ongoing aspect.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

**The correct sentence should be:** *Soumya will speak on 'Stress management' in London next week.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**on 'Stress Management' in**" is grammatically correct as it is a preposition followed by a noun phrase.
 
• "**London the next week**" is also grammatically correct as it is a prepositional phrase indicating time and place.

questions.question:
**Direction: Read the sentence to find out whether there is any grammatical error in it. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. Spot the error from the given options.**

This candidate lacks (a)/ an experience (b)/ otherwise (c)/ he is well qualified (d).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'b.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in Part (b) of the sentence.
 
• **Abstract nouns** refer to abstract ideas – things that do not physically exist, such as love, honesty, knowledge, education or friendship.
 
• Most abstract nouns are uncountable, and we do not use articles when we talk about things in general.
 
 
• **Example**: *I think education is the most essential factor in life.*
 
 
 
• The noun** "experience"** is an abstract noun.
 
• Therefore, the use of 'an experience' in part b should be replaced with **'experience'** to make it grammatically correct.
 
• Correct sentence__: *This candidate lacks** experience** otherwise he is well qualified.*

 

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** *

__
 
• You should use the phrase “if I was…” when referring to something that actually happened.

 
 
• Example: *If I was late for curfew when I was a teenager, my parents grounded me.*
 
 

 

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__** *

 
• त्रुटि वाक्य के Part (b) में है।
 
• Abstract nouns अमूर्त विचारों को संदर्भित करती हैं - ऐसी चीजें जो शारीरिक रूप से मौजूद नहीं हैं, जैसे कि प्यार, ईमानदारी, ज्ञान, शिक्षा या दोस्ती।
 
• अधिकांश Abstract nouns, uncountable होती हैं, और जब हम सामान्य रूप से चीजों के बारे में बात करते हैं तो हम लेखों का उपयोग नहीं करते हैं।
 
 
• Example: *I think education is the most essential factor in life.*
 
 
 
• Noun "experience" एक abstract noun है।
 
• इसलिए, भाग b में **'an experience'** के प्रयोग को व्याकरण की दृष्टि से सही बनाने के लिए 'experience' से प्रतिस्थापित किया जाना चाहिए।

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate form of the tense / tense sequence.

By the time he returned, I ______ ten pages of my report.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'had typed'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence uses** a past perfect tense **to describe an action that was completed before another action in the past.
 
• The **past perfect** is made from the verb had and the **past participle of a verb.**
 
 
• **​Example:** I **had finished** the work. She had gone.
 
 
 
• In this context, by the time he returned, the typing of ten pages was already completed.__
 
• The past perfect tense is formed using "**had**" followed by the past participle of the verb, which in this case is "**typed**."

**Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• "**typed**" (Option 1) is in simple past tense, which doesn't convey the sequence of actions.
 
• "**typing**" (Option 2) is a present participle and does not fit the tense structure of the sentence.
 
• "**would have been typing**" (Option 4) indicates a conditional continuous action that would have happened but did not, which is not the intended meaning here.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.**

My father promised __to be bringing__ a new mobile phone for me.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **to bring**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Replace **"to be bringing"** with **"to bring"** to make the sentence correct.
 
• "**Promise**" means to say definitely that you will give something to somebody.
 
• The given sentence is written in the Future perfect simple tense. We use the future perfect simple to talk about something that will be completed before a specific time in the future.
 
• Here, '**to**' is used to show that something must happen or that something has been arranged.
 
• '**bringing**' is used in the continuous tense. so it will be grammatically incorrect to use it in the given sentence.
 
• With "**promise**" immediately followed by a verb, we use the infinitive, **"to+ verb1" not "-ing".**
 
 
• **Example -** *The college principal **promised to look** into the matter.*
 
 

*​*Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

**Corrected sentence: ***My father **promised to bring__** a new mobile phone for me. *

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

The barking of dogs woke up the residents of the slum.

options.text: The residents of the slum were woken up by the barking of dogs.
The residents of the slum had been woken up by the barking of dogs.
The residents of the slum are waking up by the barking of dogs.
The residents of the slum have woken up by the barking of dogs.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **The residents of the slum were woken up by the barking of dogs. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The Active Voice describes a sentence where the subject performs the action stated by the verb. While in the Passive Voice subject is acted upon by the verb.
 
• The given sentence is written in the **active form** of **simple past tense**.
 
• The structure of active voice = **Subject + past participle + object**__
 
• The structure of passive Voice = **__Subject + was/were + past participle + by object__**
 
• Rules of Conversion from Active to Passive Voice:
 
 
• Identify the subject, the verb, and the object.
 
• Change the object into the subject.
 
• Change the verb into the past participle of the verb.
 
• Change the subject into an object.
 
 

Thus the passive voice will be: *The residents of the slum were woken up by the barking of dogs. *

Given below are six sentences, out of which sentences A and F are in the correct position. Sentences B, C, D and E are in a jumbled order. Select the option that gives the correct order.

A. With the discovery of a southeast Greenland population in 2022,

B. but DNA studies show that they are not reproductively isolated.

C. The subpopulations display seasonal fidelity to particular areas,

D. The 14 North American subpopulations range from the Beaufort Sea south to Hudson Bay and

F. east to eastern Greenland and account for about 54% of the global population.

__
 
• In the given Para Jumble, Statement A and Statement F are fixed. Now we have to arrange the rest four statements contextually or grammatically.

 
 
• **Sentence E** will be the first sentence because it is directly connected with the introductory part of sentence A. Here, discovery is about polar bears.
 
• **Sentence C** will be the second sentence because the sentence is talking about the seasonal fidelity of polar bears.
 
• **Sentence B** will be the third sentence because it completes the meaning of statement C.
 
• Lastly,** Sentence D** will be used.

questions.question:
**Directions**: This question consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences in each have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly.

S1: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has announced a 25 basis point increase in the benchmark interest rate, the first hike in four years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**R Q P S**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sentence **R** logically follows S1 because it explains the reason behind the RBI's decision to increase the benchmark interest rate.
 
• Sentence **Q** comes next as it discusses the public and economic reactions to the decision mentioned in R.
 
• Sentence **P** follows by elaborating on the possible impact of the rate hike on different sectors of the economy.
 
• Sentence **S** naturally precedes S6 because both discuss the RBI's future approach and monitoring of the economic situation.
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is **R → Q → P → S**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **R Q P S**.

**Correct Passage:**

*"The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has announced a 25 basis point increase in the benchmark interest rate, the first hike in four years.*

***The decision, which was widely expected, was taken to curb rising inflation and stabilize the rupee, which has fallen sharply against the U.S. dollar in recent months.**__*

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no: 3.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. taken.

The passage is about how climate change is causing the depletion of glaciers in the Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9e59515216b9476fa532cbc3eb3527a04b512a54b2e424629c5adc57a4a85bcb.png] **__Explanation__**

__
 
• The auxiliary verb '**have**' is used before the blank. This means that the main verb in the blank should be in its **past participle form**.
 
• 'Has/have + past participle' is the **present perfect tense**. 
 
• Other options are rejected because:
 
 
• 'Takes' is the third-person singular simple present tense.
 
• 'Taking' is a present participle or -ing verb form of 'take' and a gerund(a verb that acts as a noun).
 
• 'Took' is the simple past tense of 'take'.
 
 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/28a00ac7d8b5f1601fa3aadee72f46847597500442a5cd21670b6c7de24bca20.png] **Mistake Point__**

__
 
• There is a possibility that the reader may get confused between **'took' and 'taken'**. But 'took' is a simple past and 'taken' is a past participle.
 
• We use the **simple past tense** for actions that began and finished in the past. Eg: *We went for a walk.*
 
• The** past participle **is not a tense. It’s a form of a verb and can’t be used on its own. You need an auxiliary verb, such as "has" or "have" or "had". Eg: *He has gone for a walk.*

**The sentence after filling the blank- ***"Based on satellite data from 1980 till 2017, several changes have **taken** place in the Rishikesh catchment area during these years."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/97a5f4f6a28d4a72e4b6b7a2f208d072ca08611a088053601b23fa83a41661f1.png] **Notes**__

 
• **Present perfect tense**: The present perfect tense refers to an action or state that either occurred at an indefinite time in the past (e.g., they have talked before) or began in the past and continued to the present time (e.g., she has grown impatient over the last hour). This tense is formed by have/has + the past participle.
 
• The** past participle** is defined by the Oxford Dictionary as “the form of a verb, typically ending in -ed in English, which is used in forming perfect and passive tenses and sometimes as an adjective.”
 
• A **present participle** is a word that (1) is formed from a verb, (2) ends in '-ing,' and (3) can be used as an adjective(eg: *crying baby*) or used to form continuous verb tenses.

• **Present perfect tense:** The present perfect tense refers to an action or state that either occurred at an indefinite time in the past (e.g., they have talked before) or began in the past and continued to the present time (e.g., she has grown impatient over the last hour). This tense is formed by **have/has + the past participle**.
 
• In the present perfect form with the **passive**, we always use** 'has/have been + the past participle form'.**
 
 
• When we use the passive form, we focus attention on what or who receives an action (the object). 
 
• ​We use the present perfect in the passive form for all the same reasons we use it in the active form – to talk about recent actions, experiences, and ongoing actions/situations.
